newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian to auction 51 pct Sidanko Jan 9.
newsitem.headline: Russian to auction 51 pct Sidanko Jan 9.

text.p: The Russian Federal Property Fund said on Tuesday it would auction 51 percent of oil company Sidanko, or 118.53 million shares, at a starting price of $129 million.
Bids for the stake will be accepted up to January 9, it said in the latest edition of its weekly Reforma bulletin.
The winner of the tender must transfer within one year a further $100 million to Sidanko to finance the development of its oil exploration and production activities, the fund said.
It must transfer a further $61 million within a year for the financial stabilisation of Sidanko.
It must also transfer 73.70 million shares in AO Angarskaya Neftekhimicheskaya Kompaniya (ANKhK), a refinery in Angara, to Sidanko. It was not immediately clear what size stake this was.
Sidanko already owns 38 percent of the refinery, or 50.7 percent of its voting shares.

OAO Sibirsko-Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Sidanko) is one of a dozen vertically integrated Russian oil groups created over the last few years. Its main operating units are Varyoganneftegaz, Kondpetroleum and Chernogorneft.
In September ZAO Interros Oil, affiliated with the Interros financial-industrial group built around Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian) won an investment tender for 34 percent of Sidanko.
MFK bank, which is associated with Uneximbank, won the right last year to manage a 51 percent stake in Sidanko under the government's shares-for-loans programme.
It appeared that this was the stake now being auctioned, as stakes transferred into external management under the rules of the programme could be sold from September this year.
